D6 (Sprint 3, individual, given 2026-11-16). Done for #62 (PR #115, see [[issue-62-design-decisions]]) and #113 (core-flows unit tests, see [[issue-113-design-decisions]]).

## Requirements
- Tool required (manual mutation doesn't count): StrykerJS with the Jest runner for Medusa. Mutate only source files changed by the PR. Commit the config used; credit a teammate if reusing their setup (reusing your own #62 setup is fine).
- Analyze every surviving mutant, plus NoCoverage ones (at least 10 if more than 10, PR-added/changed lines first): equivalent or test gap, and why.
- Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a gap survivor; re-run to confirm. If none are gaps, justify in the table.
- Evidence: JSON reports committed as docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue>-njpiombino-before.json and -after.json. Scores must match the reports (score = killed+timeout / all mutants, NoCoverage counts against); the killed mutant must show Killed in "after".
- Submission: docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue>-njpiombino.md with template: title "# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <title>"; header **PR(s):** **Tool:** **Config:** **Command:**; **Reports:** before/after links; **Mutation score:** before% -> after%; "## Surviving mutants" table | Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |; "## New or strengthened test" Commit · Test (file › name) · Kills; "## Questions" 1) what survivors revealed, 2) any survivor pointing to an assertion whose expected value wasn't from requirements, 3) AI use: what it produced and what was verified/corrected (or N/A). Q3 ends with a "Verified by me:" line the user supplies; the user must rerun Stryker themselves before submitting.
- The PR description's Test Evidence also links the D6 doc and gives the score (see [[pr-description-format]]).

## Working setup (from #62; reuse)
- Root dev deps already installed: `@stryker-mutator/core` and `@stryker-mutator/jest-runner` 10.1.1. `.gitignore` already ignores `.stryker-tmp` and `packages/modules/inventory/reports/mutation` (add the new package's reports dir).
- Config lives in the package dir: `packages/modules/inventory/stryker.config.json` + `stryker-build.cjs`. Copy both to the next package and change `mutate` (use a line range like `src/x.ts:443-553` to mutate only PR lines) and the file path in stryker-build.cjs. Run: `cd <package> && npx stryker run` with Postgres up (localhost:5433). About 7 min for 72 mutants and 48 tests.
- Key settings and why:
  - `testRunner: "jest"`, `jest.projectType: "custom"`, `configFile: "jest.config.js"`, a `testMatch` for the integration tests, `enableFindRelatedTests: false`.
  - Module integration tests load `dist/`, not `src/`, so `buildCommand` must rebuild after instrumentation. `buildCommand` is not run through a shell (`&&` breaks), so point it at a script.
  - `inPlace: true`: the sandbox copy breaks the package tsconfig's relative `extends`.
  - `coverageAnalysis: "all"`: `moduleIntegrationTestRunner` wraps suites in `describe("")`, so perTest coverage ids never match Jest test names and every mutant shows NoCoverage.
  - `concurrency: 1`: test runs share one DB name.
- Babel bug (both Stryker 10/Babel 8 and Stryker 9/Babel 7.29): instrumentation drops parameter decorators on params with a default value, so `@MedusaContext() context: Context = {}` loses its decorator and @EmitEvents tests fail in the initial run ("reading 'messageAggregator'"). `stryker-build.cjs` re-adds `@MedusaContext()` via regex before `yarn build`. Check that the target service uses the same `context: Context = {}` param name (some use `sharedContext`); adjust the regex if so.
- HTTP integration tests (`integration-tests/http`) can't be used: they boot a server against built packages. Mirror their cases as module-level tests so Stryker can see them.

## Core-flows recipe (#113; much simpler)
- `packages/core/core-flows/stryker.config.json`: jest runner, `projectType: custom`, `testMatch` of the unit spec files, `mutate` the pure util files, `inPlace: true` (sandbox breaks jest.config.js's relative require of define_jest_config), `coverageAnalysis: perTest` works (normal describe names). No build, no DB. ~2-3 min per run. Reports dir `packages/core/core-flows/reports/mutation` is gitignored.
- Put logic in pure functions with unit tests so Stryker can see it; workflows/steps/HTTP tests are too slow to mutate.
- Format (prettier) BEFORE the final before/after runs, or report line numbers won't match committed code. To redo "before", remove only the new tests and restore weakened assertions.
- RuntimeError mutants (e.g. BigInt mixing) are excluded from the score; say so in the doc.

## After each run
- Check `grep -c stryNS` in src and dist is 0. If dist is instrumented, rebuild the package (`yarn workspace <pkg> build`).
- Delete `src/migrations/.snapshot-*-integration-1.json`, which module test runs generate.
- Copy `reports/mutation/mutation.json` to the docs reports path; recompute scores from the JSON.
- A python snippet over `files[*].mutants` (status, location, replacement, and the source span) is the fastest way to list survivors with their original code.

## Typical #62 findings (for analysis)
Equivalent survivors were performance shortcuts (early returns on empty lists, narrowing a query to ids already filtered in memory, `select: ["id"]`). Real gaps were edge cases: first page with `take`, zero DB matches, caller's relations/select passed through, multiple invalid values in an error message. Removing equivalent shortcuts to raise the score was rejected (makes code worse).

**Why:** Graded deliverable that repeats for the next issue; setup took several failed runs to get right.
**How to apply:** Start from this recipe instead of rediscovering it; check the new package's test loader and decorator param names first.
DB_UP

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: run-suites.sh <label>  -- builds changed packages at current checkout, runs suites, logs to scratchpad/<label>/
set -u
OUT="$(dirname "$0")/$1"; mkdir -p "$OUT"
cd /workspaces/medusa
J=/workspaces/medusa/node_modules/.bin/jest
for p in @medusajs/types @medusajs/js-sdk @medusajs/inventory @medusajs/order @medusajs/core-flows @medusajs/medusa; do
  yarn workspace $p build > "$OUT/build-${p#@medusajs/}.log" 2>&1 || echo "BUILD FAIL $p" >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
done
run() { # name dir cmd...
  local name=$1 dir=$2; shift 2
  ( cd "$dir" && timeout 3600 "$@" ) > "$OUT/$name.log" 2>&1
  echo "$name: $(grep -E '^Tests:|Tests +[0-9]' "$OUT/$name.log" | tail -1)" >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
}
run inventory-unit packages/modules/inventory $J --forceExit --testPathPattern=src
run inventory-integ packages/modules/inventory $J --forceExit --testPathPattern='integration-tests/__tests__/.*\.spec\.ts'
run order-unit packages/modules/order $J --forceExit --testPathPattern=src
run order-integ packages/modules/order $J --forceExit --testPathPattern='integration-tests/__tests__/.*\.spec\.ts'
run core-flows-unit packages/core/core-flows $J --forceExit --passWithNoTests
run js-sdk-unit packages/core/js-sdk $J --forceExit --passWithNoTests
run medusa-unit packages/medusa $J --forceExit --testPathIgnorePatterns=/integration-tests/ --testPathPattern=src
run dashboard-unit packages/admin/dashboard /workspaces/medusa/node_modules/.bin/vitest --run
for d in inventory reservations product cart order workflow-engine; do
  run http-$d integration-tests/http $J --no-cache --forceExit --testPathPattern="__tests__/$d/"
done
run modules-cart integration-tests/modules $J --no-cache --forceExit --testPathPattern="__tests__/cart/"
echo DONE >> "$OUT/summary.txt"

```

Use `specstory sync`. Run it from the project folder:

```bash
cd /workspaces/medusa
specstory sync claude
```

That converts every Claude Code session for this project (the ones in `~/.claude/projects/-workspaces-medusa/`) into markdown in [.specstory/history/](.specstory/history/). Plain `specstory sync` does the same for every agent it finds, not just Claude. Sessions that are already there get updated, not duplicated.

This container only has one Claude Code project. If you have others somewhere else, run the same command once inside each project folder, because SpecStory goes one project at a time.

Two settings in [.specstory/cli/config.toml](.specstory/cli/config.toml) are worth knowing:
- `local_time_zone = true` names files by your local time instead of UTC.
- If you're logged in to SpecStory, sessions also upload to SpecStory Cloud by default; set `[cloud_sync] enabled = false` or pass `--no-cloud-sync` to stop that.

The `specstory` command isn't installed in this container (`command not found`), even though [.specstory/history/](.specstory/history/) already has 28 sessions. You probably ran it from your host machine or another terminal, so run the command there too. I took the command from SpecStory's usage pattern and didn't run it here; if a flag doesn't match your version, `specstory sync --help` shows the exact options.
